definition_zh: 通过概率密度随动力过程的演化研究随机响应分布的方法。
definition_en: A method that tracks the evolution of probability density in stochastic dynamical systems using probability conservation.
usage_overview: 基于概率守恒，利用动力响应轨迹将随机输入的概率信息传递到随时间变化的响应概率密度，连接确定性动力计算与随机响应评价。在车辆—轨道等耦合系统中，用于分析随机激励下的响应分布，也用作其他随机分析方法的比较基准。

complete_examples.text: Furthermore, the probability density evolution method was applied to solve the delivery problem of probabilities between excitation inputs and response outputs.

Based on the principle of probability conservation, a probability density evolution method (PDEM) used to capture the flow trajectories of probabilities for linear/nonlinear stochastic systems has been presented by Li and Chen [32] , and a series of applications can be found in Refs. [32–34] .
Moreover, the probabilistic transmission relationships between track irregularities and system responses are addressed by introducing a probability density evolution method.

In addition, the vehicle–track coupled model, probability density evolution method (PDEM) and random process theory are modelled and introduced for obtaining the dynamic responses and capturing the probabilistic transmission between track random irregularities and dynamic responses.
PDEM is a newly developed method applied to capture the probabilistic features, particu-larly PDF, of the linear or nonlinear dynamic system through the trajectories of dynamic responses [30].

Finally, a probability density evolution method (PDEM) is introduced to solve the probabilistic transmission issues between track irregularity sets and dynamic responses of vehicle–track coupled systems.

Additionally, it is worth mentioning that more and more researchers began to pay attention to the random vibrations of railway dynamics, see for instance, Xu and Zhai [18] proposed a computational model to analyze the temporal–spatial stochastic vibrations of vehicle–track systems, in which the randomness of system parameters and excitations are effectively considered and coupled; Mao et al. [19] introduced the probability density evolution method (PDEM) into the random analysis of train–bridge coupled system involving random system parameters; Zhu et al. [20] and Zeng et al. [21] studies the stochastic vibration of vehicle–bridge system using pseudo-excitation method (PEM) by mainly considering the random characteristics of track irregularities.

Furthermore, a vehicle-track coupled model is presented to obtain the dynamic responses of vehicle-track systems due to the earthquakes and track random irregularities at time-domain, and the probability density evolution method (PDEM) is introduced to describe the evolutionary process of probability from excitation input to response output by assuming the vehicle-track system as a probabilistic conservative system, which lays the foundation on reliability assessment of vehicle-track systems.

Secondly, a vehicle-track coupled model that properly considers the wheel-rail nonlinear contacts and the excitations of seismic waves is developed, in which a probability density evolution method (PDEM) [23] is introduced to solve the probabilistic transmission between excitation inputs and response outputs.

To assess the dynamic performance of a railway system in more comprehensive and practical ways, a framework for probabilistic assessment of vehicle-curved track systems is developed by effectively integrating a vehicle–track coupled model (VTCM), a track irregularity probabilistic model (TIPM) with a probability density evolution method (PDEM).

Lastly, PDEM, a newly developed method for solving probabilistic transmissions between stochastic excitations and deterministic dynamic responses, is introduced to this probabilistic assessment model.
The stochastic fractional derivative model is based on the Gru ̈nwald representation of fractional calculus, the number theoretical method, and the probability density evolution method (PDEM).

Keywords Floating slab track, vibration isolation performance, fractional derivative, stochastic analysis, vehicle–track coupled dynamics, number theoretical method, probability density evolution method Date received: 13 October 2018; accepted: 15 September 2019 Introduction Due to the advantages of large capacity, speed and punctuality, and the ability to significantly alleviate traffic congestion as well as pollution in urban areas,1 the metro system has been one of the most popular solutions for large cities in order to deal with urban transportation problems.

Following the pioneering work in [34–36], Li and Chen [7] made strides in the development of a family of probability density evolution method based on the principle of probability preservation and its random event description, in which a unified logic foundation for characterizing the randomness propagations is laid on.

From aspects of systematic dynamics and by introducing method-ologies above, Mao et al. [38] conducted a work in random dynamic analysis for a train–bridge system based on probability density evolution method, where random system parameters and track irregularities are considered, while the longitudinal inhomogeneity of the system property and the probabilistic ergodicity of track irregularities accumu-lated from a long time measurement are not considered completely.
基于随机分析理论,考虑线路不平顺及系统动力参数的时-空随机演变特性,将车辆-轨道耦合动力学理论与概率密度演化方法结合,提出一种用于线路基础结构伤损识别的概率密度分布演化方法。
本文基于随机分析的一般理论,考虑线路不平顺的空间随机性和长时效演变性,以及轨道结构动力参数的随机性,将车辆-轨道耦合动力学理论 [3]与概率密度演化方法 [4]结合,提出一种用于铁路线路基础结构伤损识别的概率密度分布演化方法。
